case_name: Alejandro J. Rojas and Elena G. Rojas v. Commissioner

taxpayer.notes: Alejandro paid 'family support' to former spouse Cristina under a 2012 Los Angeles Superior Court stipulated judgment. Submitted fully stipulated under Rule 122.

notice_of_deficiency.contested_by_taxpayer: Disallowance of alimony deduction for family support payments

findings_of_fact.fact: Alejandro and Cristina married 1995, separated 2010, divorced 2012; judgment of dissolution entered July 25, 2012
findings_of_fact.snippet: On July 25, 2012, the Los Angeles Superior Court (L.A. Superior Court) entered a judgment of dissolution,

findings_of_fact.fact: Stipulated judgment: no child or spousal support; family support of $4,500 per month payable by Alejandro to Cristina
findings_of_fact.snippet: family support shall be payable by Respondent [Alejandro] to Petitioner [Cristina] in the monthly amount of $4,500.00 payable on the 1st of each month.

findings_of_fact.fact: Family support commences Aug. 1, 2011 and continues until both minor children emancipate or Cristina remarries; on remarriage reduced to $2,500/month until each child emancipates
findings_of_fact.snippet: Such support order commences August 1, 2011 and is continuing until both minor children emancipate or Petitioner remarries.

findings_of_fact.fact: During 2016 Alejandro made 12 monthly payments of $5,824 each, total $69,888
findings_of_fact.snippet: During 2016 Alejandro made 12 monthly payments of $5,824 each to Cristina, for a total of $69,888.

findings_of_fact.fact: Petitioners deducted $69,880 as alimony on 2016 joint return
findings_of_fact.snippet: petitio ners deducted $69,880 as alimony payments .

findings_of_fact.fact: Feb. 11, 2014 L.A. Superior Court order denied downward modification RFO and found no current child support order
findings_of_fact.snippet: On February 11, 2014, the L.A. Superior Court denied the RFO without prejudice,

issues.question: May petitioners deduct under sec. 215 the 2016 family support payments that terminate when both minor children emancipate or the payee remarries?
issues.holding: No; termination on child emancipation is a child-related contingency under sec. 71(c)(2)(A) regardless of the additional spouse-related contingency, so the payments are treated as child support, not includible by payee and not deductible; state court labels and Full Faith and Credit argument rejected; no equitable relief
issues.computable_reason: Instrument terms (payment reduces/ends on child emancipation) mechanically trigger sec. 71(c)(2)(A); pre-2019 instrument so secs. 71/215 apply

decision.text: An appropriate decision will be entered.
decision.summary: Alimony deduction disallowed (deficiency sustained); 6662(a) penalty conceded by respondent

notes: Submitted under Rule 122. Payments of $5,824/month exceeded the $4,500 required amount; record silent why (fn. 2). $8 discrepancy between $69,880 deducted and $69,888 paid unexplained (fn. 3). Under Cal. law family support is unallocated child and spousal support (Cal. Fam. Code §92). Whole amount disallowed, not just a reduction amount, since payments end on child emancipation.
